mechanism_narrative: The steady decline in WORKPLACES mobility, combined with only partial recovery in TRANSIT, will keep weekday foot traffic weak and pull RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks because commuting-linked shopping trips remain suppressed.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days rises above the last 28-day mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both continue to weaken or stay flat.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and WORKPLACES remain depressed, more activity is shifted into home-based routines and discretionary shopping outside the home falls, producing lower RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 8 points while WORKPLACES stays below -20 points for at least two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL remains high and WORKPLACES remains below -20 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp improvement in PARKS mobility signals a broader easing of local movement constraints and spillover into shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC will rise over the next four weeks as outdoor activity normalizes.
failure_condition: PARKS continues to improve but RETAIL_REC remains below the prior 28-day mean over the following 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT drops back more than five points week-on-week, that indicates renewed access friction or restrictions that reduce shopping access, and RETAIL_REC will decline within one week.
failure_condition: A week-on-week fall in TRANSIT of more than 5 points is followed by a stable or higher RETAIL_REC in the next 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in GROCERY_PHARM alongside rising RESIDENTIAL implies fewer essential out-of-home errands, which will spill over into weaker discretionary shopping and push RETAIL_REC down over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM staying below -10 and RESIDENTIAL staying above 9.

mechanism_narrative: Because PARKS is near zero while RETAIL_REC is still deeply negative, the city is moving from outdoor leisure into indoor consumption; this lagged substitution should lift retail activity over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -10 while RETAIL_REC remains below -25
failure_condition: PARKS rises above -10 without a subsequent increase in RETAIL_REC over the following 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a restriction-easing regime, simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES creates a commuting recovery channel that raises retail visits; the effect appears within two weeks and is strongest when both series improve together.
failure_condition: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM keeps recovering while WORKPLACES stay negative, the mix of local errand mobility and reduced commuting will shift spending back toward neighborhood retail, producing a modest RETAIL_REC increase over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -10 while WORKPLACES remains below -20
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM improves above -10 and WORKPLACES stays below -20, yet RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days.
